parsed.headline: Syria's Foreign Ministry condemns Houthi drone attack on Medina power station

pages.text: Syria’s Foreign Ministry issued a condemnation on Friday regarding a Houthi drone attack on a power distribution station located in Medina, Saudi Arabia. According to the North Press Agency, the ministry stated that the strike targeted civilian infrastructure. The station in question provides electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.
The ministry further asserted that the attack on the station violated Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and threatened regional stability.

parsed.headline: NPP delegates to elect national leadership in Kumasi

pages.text: More than 7,000 delegates are expected to convene at the Baba Yara Stadium in Kumasi to elect new national leadership for the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and determine the party's organizational direction ahead of the 2028 general election. The National Delegates Congress is scheduled for September 26, 2026, and will involve 47 aspirants contesting nine national executive positions across 31 polling stations. The positions to be filled include National Chairperson, General Secretary, three Vice-Chairpersons, National Treasurer, National Organiser, National Women’s Organiser, and National Youth Organiser. The conference is structured in two parts: delegates will consider proposed constitutional amendments starting at 9 a.m., with voting scheduled to begin at noon. Proposed amendments, which may include fewer than 20 items, involve matters such as the designation of the party leader and the method for electing Vice Chairpersons.

The contest for National Chairperson includes John Boadu, Sammy Crabbe, Paul Afoko, and Boakye Agyarko. According to the ballot, Mr. Boadu is listed first, followed by Mr. Crabbe, Mr. Afoko, and Mr. Agyarko. While an Africa Policy Lens and Global Info Analytics poll placed Mr. Boadu in the lead, other surveys produced varying results, making the chairmanship a close contest. In the General Secretary race, incumbent Justin Kodua Frimpong faces Eugene Boakye Antwi, Sylvester Tetteh, and former National Treasurer Charles Dwamena. The choice of Kumasi, the Ashanti Regional capital, places the party's grassroots organization at the center of the leadership transition following its 2024 electoral defeat.

parsed.headline: Stan Dogbe clarifies beachfront demolition near Labadi Beach Hotel was at hotel's request

pages.text: Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations, Stan Dogbe, has clarified that a demolition of structures along a section of the beachfront near the Labadi Beach Hotel on Friday was not part of the government’s flood mitigation exercise. According to Mr. Dogbe, the operation was carried out under the supervision of National Security at the request of the Labadi Beach Hotel. The demolition included the Polo Beach Club as security personnel continued a clearance exercise around the La beachfront. The operation involved personnel from the Ghana Police Service and the 48 Engineer Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces.

Mr. Dogbe stated in a Facebook post that the operation was separate from the National Flood Mitigation Task Force, which is currently operating around Oyarifa, East Legon Boundary Road, Kpeshie Lagoon, and behind Mayfair Estates to support the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources. He noted that the affected structures were located on the beachfront in front of the hotel and, according to the hotel, were adversely affecting its reputation, tranquillity, safety, and the visitor experience. Mr. Dogbe added that the hotel would be better positioned to provide specific details regarding its request to reclaim the beachfront, though he raised concerns regarding security risks and sanitation issues stemming from unauthorized and unregulated commercial operations along the beach.

parsed.headline: President Mahama attributes Hohoe flooding to climate change-linked extreme weather

pages.text: President John Mahama has linked recent flooding in the Hohoe Municipality to extreme weather patterns associated with climate change, stating that changing rainfall patterns are making weather prediction increasingly difficult. The President made these remarks during a visit to communities affected by the disaster to present relief items to displaced residents. The flooding, which was triggered by the overflow of the River Dayi following heavy rains, affected more than 5,000 people and hundreds of homes in the municipality. According to the President, heavy rainfall in neighboring Togo sent large volumes of water into the River Dayi, causing it to overflow and flood low-lying areas in Hohoe. He noted that climate change is leading to extreme weather phenomena, characterized by periods of excessive rainfall followed by drought, making weather behavior less predictable.

During his visit, President Mahama presented relief supplies including mattresses and bags of rice. Additionally, Dzata Cement has pledged 5,000 bags of cement to assist residents whose homes were destroyed by the floods. The President stated he learned of the disaster while returning from attending the United Nations in New York and decided to visit the affected communities to support relief efforts. He acknowledged the response efforts of traditional leaders, Zongo chiefs, the Member of Parliament, the Municipal Chief Executive, and the presiding member.

parsed.headline: Netanyahu claims Omani co-pilot in flight stabbing had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination

pages.text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed that an Omani co-pilot who stabbed his captain during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination and was suicidal. The incident occurred on September 30, 2026, when the aircraft plunged more than 17,000 feet (5,200 meters) approximately two hours into its journey. Israeli passengers intervened to restrain the co-pilot, while a reserve crew stabilized the plane, allowing it to land safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The plane had more than 170 people onboard. Israeli officials announced that four passengers would receive a “heroism” award for their role in preventing a potential disaster. Following the emergency landing, the co-pilot was arrested by Saudi security services and is being interrogated. Netanyahu told Fox News that preliminary indications suggest the attacker was likely attempting to down the plane, noting that once subdued, the individual was calling out to the aircrew to 'kill me.' While Netanyahu cited radicalization as a potential clue, he emphasized that final conclusions regarding motive have yet to be made.

Investigations into the motive behind the attack are being conducted by Saudi investigators in cooperation with the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Oman, and Israel. A regional official told the Associated Press that all scenarios, ranging from terrorism to mental disorders, are being examined. The UAE state news agency reported that investigations have begun to determine if the incident was linked to terrorist activity. While two Israeli security officials stated their initial assessment was that the co-pilot was likely acting alone, US President Donald Trump and UAE officials have indicated to the media that Iran may be responsible, though they have not definitively blamed Tehran. Netanyahu previously stated it was too early to confirm if there was state backing from Iran, and two Israeli security sources told Reuters they had not yet found evidence of Iranian involvement. The Saudi Interior Ministry stated that both the pilot and co-pilot were sent back to the UAE after being cleared by medical teams.

parsed.headline: Sydney Hushie appointed Chief of the Digital Centre of Excellence at UNFPA headquarters

pages.text: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) has appointed Ghanaian Sydney Hushie as the Chief of the Digital Centre of Excellence at the organization's headquarters in New York. The appointment was made by the Executive Director of the Fund and United Nations Under-Secretary-General, Ms. Diene Keita. In this leadership role, Mr. Hushie will oversee the unit responsible for utilizing digital innovation, data, emerging technologies, and institutional systems to advance the organization's mandate across its regional and country offices. The UNFPA's mission includes working to end preventable maternal deaths, meeting unmet needs for family planning, and ending gender-based violence and harmful practices. Mr. Hushie's role involves managing digital tools, such as data systems for decision-making and technologies used to extend the reach of health services, to support these objectives for women, girls, and young people worldwide. Prior to this appointment, Mr. Hushie spent six years at the UNFPA's East and Southern Africa Regional Office in Johannesburg, where he led the region's innovation and digital transformation portfolio. His work in that region included overseeing projects such as the introduction of medical drones for maternal health commodity delivery, the use of virtual reality for health worker training, the deployment of artificial intelligence-powered point-of-care ultrasound devices, and the mobilization of innovation financing from private partners, development banks, and governments. Mr. Hushie's professional background includes experience in development finance and innovation, with previous roles at the African Development Bank and the British Council and professional experience spanning more than 20 countries.

parsed.headline: Toronto Region Board of Trade urges provincial reform of zoning and building codes

pages.text: The Toronto Region Board of Trade is calling on the Ontario provincial government to amend zoning and building code rules, stating that the province is on pace to fall short of its goal to build at least 1.5 million new homes by 2031. In a report published Thursday, the board asserted that the target, established by the provincial government in 2022, is unachievable by the current deadline even if housing production increases over the next five years. According to the board's analysis of budget forecasts, Ontario is projected to fall more than 550,000 homes short of the pace required by 2029. Board president and CEO Giles Gherson described existing zoning and building code rules as out of date and fragmented across the province. Gherson noted that in Toronto, builders face dozens of different requirements, which he stated adds cost and delay to development. The board indicated that even if reforms were adopted immediately, the time required for municipalities to update plans, amend zoning bylaws, align infrastructure, service land, and process applications could make the 2031 goal unrealistic.

parsed.headline: President Mahama visits Global Mercy hospital ship at Tema Port

pages.text: On October 1, 2026, President John Dramani Mahama welcomed the crew and medical staff of the Global Mercy hospital ship at Tema Port in the Greater Accra Region. Accompanied by Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh and other senior government officials, the President was received by Dame Ann Gloag, the Lifetime Director of Mercy Ships International. The vessel is scheduled to remain in the country for a 10-month mission to provide free specialized surgeries and dental care to Ghanaians. During the visit, the President toured various departments and interacted with patients, including children who had undergone orthopedic surgeries. President Mahama noted that bringing the ship to Ghana involved complex conditions precedent and praised Ms. Gloag for her persistence in managing the mission's arrival.

President Mahama directed the Ministry of Health to collaborate with Mercy Ships on professional training, patient referrals, and follow-up care to ensure medical support continues after the ship departs. He stated that Ghanaian surgeons, nurses, and anesthesia professionals would have the opportunity to train alongside the Global Mercy team. The President also directed sector ministries and agencies to coordinate on medical supplies, patient movement, and operational arrangements. Addressing challenges, the President noted that Dame Ann Gloag had apprised him of two specific issues facing the mission, which he pledged to resolve. He acknowledged Mercy Ships' history in Ghana, noting that four previous missions since 1991 delivered more than 2,600 surgeries, 16,700 dental procedures, and supported the development of 139 Ghanaian health professionals.

parsed.headline: Lebanese army seizes explosives and detonators smuggled from Syria

pages.text: The Lebanese Army reported on Thursday that it seized approximately 245 kilograms of TNT, four explosive devices, eight detonators, and electrical wires used for detonating explosives. According to a statement from the army, the materials were being smuggled from Syria into Lebanon during monitoring operations conducted along the northern and eastern borders. The army stated that smugglers fled toward Syrian territory following the arrival of an army patrol at the site. The Lebanese Army conducts regular surveillance and security operations along its borders with Syria to monitor smuggling and prevent the movement of weapons and explosives.

parsed.headline: Two Luv 99.5FM journalists selected for UK MEET fellowship

pages.text: Clinton Yeboah and Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom, journalists with the Kumasi unit of the Multimedia Group, have been selected for the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technology (UK MEET) Fellowship. According to MyJoyOnline, the two Luv 99.5FM journalists were chosen from more than 500 applications submitted by journalists and content creators across Ghana and Nigeria, placing them among the 13 percent of applicants admitted to the programme. The selection process involved independent assessments by two reviewers who evaluated candidates based on reporting records, clarity of perspective, and story pitches regarding investigative questions. The fellowship is delivered by Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana, with support from the British High Commission, and aims to strengthen journalism regarding science, technology, and emerging innovations.

The programme is scheduled to begin with residential training in Accra, where fellows will engage with researchers in fields such as artificial intelligence, health technology, and climate change. Participants are set to receive practical training in verifying information, scrutinizing scientific and technological claims, identifying relevant data, and translating complex developments into accessible stories. Additionally, the fellowship will include editorial clinics to assist fellows in refining story ideas, strengthening sources, and developing publication strategies. Beyond the training components, the fellowship seeks to build professional networks among science and technology journalists across the region to facilitate collaboration and knowledge-sharing.

parsed.headline: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia following embassy closure and diplomat expulsion

pages.text: Eritrea announced it was severing all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia on October 1, 2026. The decision by Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed an announcement from Addis Ababa that it would close its embassy in Asmara and expel 10 Eritrean diplomats. Eritrea stated the move was a reciprocation of Ethiopia's actions, which it described as an “agenda of incessant hostility” involving the infringement on coastal areas and the arming of fighters opposed to the Eritrean government. Both nations have rejected mutual accusations of backing armed groups opposed to their respective governments. Ethiopia has also expelled an Egyptian diplomat, providing 48 hours for departure, though the government has not publicly stated a reason for that decision. Al Jazeera reports that the diplomatic breakdown follows months of worsening relations driven by disputes over Ethiopia's push for Red Sea access and allegations that Eritrea is backing the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival fighting in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia has further accused Egypt and Sudan of joining Eritrea in supporting Tigrayan rebel forces. Analysts warn that the unrest could potentially destabilize Sudan and spill into neighboring states.

Renewed fighting has emerged in northern Ethiopia between federal troops and an opposition alliance across parts of the Tigray, Afar, and Amhara regions. BBC World reports that more than 50 people have been killed since heavy fighting resumed in northern Ethiopia last week. These clashes are described as the most severe in Ethiopia since the 2020-2022 civil war, which resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths. The fighting involves Ethiopian federal forces battling fighters from the TPLF and its allies, an alliance that Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of supporting.

parsed.headline: Saudi Arabia reports Flydubai co-pilot assaulted captain during flight to Tel Aviv

pages.text: Saudi Arabia announced on October 1, 2026, that a Flydubai co-pilot assaulted the captain during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, resulting in an emergency landing in Tabuk. According to the Saudi Interior Ministry, preliminary investigations conducted alongside a UAE security team found that the assault left both pilots with injuries. Flydubai flight FZ1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion International Airport on September 30, 2026, before being granted permission to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk. The aircraft landed safely at 9:45 a.m. local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members on board. Following the landing, Saudi authorities provided assistance to those on board. All passengers continued their journey at 5:40 p.m. via a replacement Flydubai aircraft, while the remaining crew returned to Dubai on another airline flight. The captain and co-pilot were hospitalized for treatment; after receiving medical clearance and showing improved conditions, they departed Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on October 1, 2026, accompanied by a UAE security team.

Flydubai previously stated that an altercation occurred inside the cockpit and that crew members secured the aircraft before diverting to Saudi Arabia. The airline noted that the causes and motives behind the incident remain unknown and are subject to an official investigation. The UAE Public Prosecution has ordered an investigation to determine if the incident was linked to terrorist activity or a pre-planned motive. Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s National Transport Safety Center has launched a separate safety investigation to collect evidence and assess aviation safety aspects regarding the incident.

parsed.headline: Niagara Falls Tourism invites Buffalo residents to red, white, and blue display

pages.text: Niagara Falls Tourism placed a full-page open letter in the Buffalo News on Friday, inviting Americans to cross the bridge to celebrate with Ontario neighbours on the night of September 26, 2026. During this event, Niagara Falls will be illuminated in the red, white, and blue colours associated with the NFL's Buffalo Bills, accompanied by matching-coloured fireworks. Adam Stiles, interim president and CEO of Niagara Falls Tourism, stated that Canadians want to return the love and spread a message of coming together during a time when tariffs and other political issues dominate the news. Stiles told CBC News, “We just want to say thank you for doing something nice for us.”
